He is an assistant coach for the [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia Bulldogs]]. Hayes was selected by the [[Washington Wizards]] with the 10th overall pick of the [[2003 NBA draft]]. == Early life and college career == Hayes was born five minutes ahead of his twin brother, [[Jonas Hayes|Jonas]].{{Cite web |last=Baum |first=Adam |title='A preacher or a politician': A story about Xavier assistant Jonas Hayes, courtesy of his twin brother, Jarvis |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/xavier/2020/02/18/xavier-coach-jonas-hayes-story-told-his-twin-brother-jarvis/4784255002/ |access-date=2026-04-09 |website=The Enquirer |language=en-US}} After attending [[Douglass High School (Atlanta)|Douglass High School]] in [[Atlanta]], he, alongside his brother, enrolled at [[Western Carolina Catamounts men's basketball|Western Carolina]], where he became the first freshman in 40 seasons to lead the [[Southern Conference]] in scoring.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}} After a year, he transferred to [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]], where he was named First Team All-SEC in both his sophomore and junior years. He became the first Bulldog to be so honored since [[Dominique Wilkins]] in 1981–82. He also stepped up in big games, averaging 28.5 points per game during the two games Georgia played in the [[2002 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2002 NCAA tournament]].{{citation needed|date=May 2021}} Hayes holds the rare distinction of having led two different conferences in scoring while in college.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}} == Professional career == === NBA career === He was taken 10th in the [[2003 NBA draft]] by the Washington Wizards, to back up [[Jerry Stackhouse]], to come in off the bench and provide that deep range. Hayes averaged 13.0 points and 4.3 rebounds through the first three games of the season but hit the 'rookie wall' within a month. He was the Wizards' only representative at the season's All-Star Weekend in Los Angeles when he made the Rookie-Sophomore challenge. By season's end, he had made through a tough season and sported some solid numbers in spite of missing 12 games with various injuries. In that rookie season, he averaged 9.6 points while making 42 starts and playing an average of 29.2 minutes.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}} Hayes did well in his second season, filling in for Larry Hughes, averaging 10.2 points a game, until a night in February when he and Manu Ginobili bumped knees. A few games later, Hayes went up for a dunk against the Sacramento Kings and when he came down, his right knee had split completely open. For a year, he hoped things would get better without surgery. In his recovery period from the injury, he ballooned to 245 pounds reviewing local area restaurants with Washingtonian Magazine Food Critic Tom Head on a weekly radio segment.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}} In his third season, at a preseason game at Wake Forest, Hayes scored 18 points in the first half of a preseason matchup with the San Antonio Spurs on Tobacco Road. After that game, his right knee, which forced him to miss a third of the 2004–05 season after he fractured his kneecap, swelled through the night. Hayes missed the remainder of the preseason. Later, on December 16, 2005, he had to leave a Laker game. The knee had fractured again and again his season was over. On February 14, 2006, he had the long-delayed surgery with the pins.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}} In the [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07 season]], he played 81 games, but only averaged 7.2 points, shot only 41% overall, but better than 36% from the three and 84.5% from the line. In the Wizards' injury plagued first round loss to the Cavs, he had started all four games, averaging 10.5 and 3.5 but shot only 32.6%. Even with a 29-point effort in the double triple-double overtime loss to the Nets in April 2007, he clearly was not the same player. Although he still had the ability to make his off-balance jump shots, he seemed to shy away from contact. From filling the lanes on the fast break as a healthy rookie he often settled for shots on the perimeter.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}} The Wizards declined to offer Hayes a contract after the 2006–07 season. On August 15, 2007, after four years with the Wizards, Hayes signed a contract for the veteran's minimum with the Detroit Pistons.[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2978003 Pistons sign free-agent forward Hayes.]. Posted August 16, 2007. Hayes became a player in the Pistons rotation, serving as the main backup for starter [[Tayshaun Prince]]. He averaged 6.7 points in 15.7 minutes, improved on his shooting numbers, and had another 29-point effort again as his best game.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}} Hayes signed with the New Jersey Nets on July 16, 2008.[http://www.nba.com/nets/news/Nets_Reach_Agreements_with_Jar-277608-64.html NETS SIGN EDUARDO NAJERA AND JARVIS HAYES.] He became the team's 6th man, he also learned to play the power forward position during the season.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}} Hayes' final NBA game was played on April 9, 2010, in a 127 - 116 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]] where he played for 9 minutes and recorded 2 points and 1 steal. === European career === In January 2011, Hayes joined the Turkish club [[Aliağa Petkim]].[http://www.aliagaekspres.com.tr/?p=4614 Jarvis Hayes, Aliağa Petkim’de {{in lang|tr}}.] In July 2011, he signed a one-year deal with [[BC Krasnye Krylya Samara]] in [[Russia]].[http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/russia/29806/krasnye_krylia_samara_agreed_to_terms_with_jarvis_hayes.html Krasnye Krylia Samara agreed to terms with Jarvis Hayes.] In February 2013, he joined the Israeli club [[Ironi Ashkelon]].{{cite news|title=Elizur Ashkelon signs former NBA Jarvis Hayes|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/israel/50630/elizur-ashkelon-signs-former-nba-jarvis-hayes.html|access-date=September 16, 2013|newspaper=Sportando.net|date=February 6, 2013}} On September 16, 2013, he signed a one-year deal with the Italian club [[Sidigas Avellino]].{{cite news|title=Sidigas Avellino announced Jarvis Hayes|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/italy/serie-a/63409/sidigas-avellino-announced-jarvis-hayes.html|access-date=September 16, 2013|newspaper=Sportando}} == Coaching career == Following his retirement from basketball, Hayes served as a TV analyst for the [[SEC Network]] and [[NBA TV]].{{Cite web |last=Blackburn |first=Gracie |date=2016-10-18 |title=Pat Bradley, Jarvis Hayes Join SEC Network as Men’s Basketball Analysts |url=https://espnpressroom.com/us/press-releases/2016/10/pat-bradley-jarvis-hayes-join-sec-network-mens-basketball-analysts/ |access-date=2026-04-09 |website=ESPN Press Room U.S. |language=en-US}} In 2018, he was hired as an assistant coach at [[Morehouse College|Morehouse]].{{Cite web |title=Morehouse hires former NBA lottery pick, UGA star as assistant coach |url=https://www.ajc.com/news/local/morehouse-hires-former-nba-lottery-pick-uga-star-assistant-coach/kFneZ4Ih0nxfNeqUhOhGtJ/ |access-date=2026-04-09 |website=ajc |language=en}} After one season at Morehouse, he was hired as an assistant at [[Georgia State Panthers men's basketball|Georgia State]], a position he served for seven seasons from 2019 to 2026.{{Cite web |last=DirtKing |first=The |date=2019-05-17 |title=Jarvis Hayes joins Georgia State Basketball Staff |url=https://hoopdirt.com/jarvis-hayes-joins-georgia-state-basketball-staff/ |access-date=2026-04-09 |website=HoopDirt |language=en-US}} On April 8, 2026, Hayes was named an assistant coach at [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]], joining the coaching staff of Bulldogs head coach [[Mike White (basketball)|Mike White]].{{Cite web |title=Georgia basketball hires former standout Jarvis Hayes as assistant coach |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/2026/04/georgia-basketball-hires-former-standout-jarvis-hayes-as-assistant-coach/ |access-date=2026-04-09 |website=ajc |language=en}} ==Qatari national team== Hayes became a naturalized citizen of [[Qatar]] in 2013 and played for the senior men's [[Qatari national basketball team]] until his retirement from basketball in 2015.{{Cite web |title=Hayes, member of 2003 draft class with LeBron, is Qatar reinforcement |url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/qatar-naturalized-player-part-of-2003-nba-draft-class-with-lebron- |access-date=2026-04-09 |website=Spin.ph |language=en}} He led the Qatar national team with 25 points, in an 87–64 win over [[Hong Kong national basketball team|Hong Kong]], during [[2013 FIBA Asia Championship Group B|group play]] of the [[2013 FIBA Asia Championship]] in Manila, Philippines.[http://www.gulf-times.com/sport/192/details/361690/qatar-top-group-in-asian-basketball Qatar top group in Asian Basketball.] ==Personal life== Hayes and his wife, Illia, were married in 2008. The couple has two sons: Jarvis Jr. and Myles.{{cite web|url=https://georgiastatesports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/coaches/jarvis-hayes/567|title=Jarvis Hayes
